For we see that if they are thrown into the **Fire**, the **Aqueous Spirit** <note>original: "Spiritum Aqueum"</note> breaks out with a crash before the **Flame** is conceived. This also happens more gently in leaves that are a little more stubborn, where the watery part breaks out before the oily part catches the **Flame**. But this is most clearly seen in **Quicksilver** <term>Argentum vivum</term> <gloss>mercury</gloss>, which is not wrongly called **Mineral Water**. This substance, without any inflammation, almost equals the force of **Gunpowder** <term>Pulvis Pyrius</term> through simple **Eruption and Expansion**; it is even said that when mixed with gunpowder, it multiplies its strength.

Similarly, let the **Nature Under Investigation** <term>Natura Inquisita</term> be the **Transitory Nature of Flame** and its **Momentary Extinction**. For the **Flaming Nature** here with us does not seem to be fixed or to stand still, but to be generated in almost every single moment and immediately extinguished. It is evident that in **Flames** which are continued and last here, that duration is not that of the same **Flame** in its **Individual** <term>Individuo</term> existence, but happens through a succession of new **Flames** generated in a series; it does not remain the same **Flame** numerically. This is easily perceived from the fact that once the **Nourishment** or **Fuel** <term>fomes</term> of the flame is withdrawn, the **Flame** immediately perishes. The **Crossroads** <term>Bivium</term> <note>a logical "Y" in the road or crucial choice between two explanations</note> concerning this nature is as follows. <summary>Bacon discusses the explosive properties of salts and mercury, then begins a "Crucial Instance" regarding the transitory nature of flame, questioning whether flame is a persistent substance or a constant succession of new moments.</summary>
